gv_leos_paintings_actors:
The actors of the dream tulip scene and the Leo's Paintings scenes (file offsets 107440-111275, bank 03): gv_npc_tulip_dream_01A3B0 (type $2A, the tulip's dream, scene A03S04) and its fairy gem gv_npc_fairy_metal_hint_01AD42, the BG2 drift actor gv_obj_bg2_scroll_drift_01B21A (type $08, every Leo's Paintings scene) and the colour gradient gv_fx_hdma_gradient_01B273 (type $0A) with its table gv_hdma_gradient_table_01B284.

=== THE TULIP'S DREAM ===
The sleeping tulip of the village that sat on the Clubhouse Pass (gv_village_actors_019475) can be entered with the Dream Rod (walkthrough: 'if you want, you can use the Dream Rod on it'). The dream tulip is registered under switch $22, the lair record of Leo's Paintings 3 (location 9, tile ($1A,$08), the Purple Birds' lair of the walkthrough) that also frees the village tulip and the boy of the secret hut. Talk: 'In my dreams I can do anything I like. For example...' 'HA!' and a gem with a fairy appears at (x $70, y $80) (COP AC with flags $50, sound $1C); later talks answer 'Why don't you try and talk to the jewelry?'. The fairy tells that the monsters in the paintings 'cannot be defeated unless you have a special sword', 'the special sword that can destroy metal' and to return when it has been found, then offers the return to Grass Valley (ReturnToGrassValleyPrompt in gv_underground_castle_actors). The walkthrough: any monster with the 'metal' attribute cannot be defeated until the Zantetsu Sword is obtained later in the game.

=== BACKGROUND AND COLOUR ===
Type $08 moves itself by (-8, -8) plus scroll_delta every frame and copies the position to the BG2 scroll registers (a fast drift of the second layer). Type $0A queues the HDMA table gv_hdma_gradient_table_01B284 for PPU register $2132 (the fixed-colour COLDATA): the first 7 lines with $F2, then 18 bands of 12 lines from $F1 down to $E0; the value is all three colour channels (bits 7-5) with an intensity of 18 falling to 0.

=== NOTES ===
- Which painting backgrounds use the BG2 drift and how fast it looks was not checked in the emulator (OQ-I034-7).
gv_multi_area_actors:
The conveyor belts of Grass Valley and one background drift actor shared by several areas (file offsets 110589-111130, bank 03): gv_obj_push_zone_setup_01AFFD (meta type $2C) picks the push zone list of the current location, seven tables of 8-byte records follow it, and gv_obj_bg2_scroll_drift_01B1F7 (type $07) drifts the second background layer.

=== PUSH ZONES ===
Type $2C is placed once in the Underground Castle scenes A02S01-S02 and in the Leo's Paintings scenes A03S01-S03 and S05-S06 (not in the dream rooms A02S03 and A03S04). It compares location_id with $05, $06, $07, $08, $09, $0B and $0C, stores the matching table in push_zone_list and its bank in push_zone_bank, and kills itself; any other location would leave the list unchanged. player_core.ScanPushZones then reads the records every frame. A record is x0, x1, y0, y1 (tiles) and the words dx, dy in pixels per frame ($0001 right or down, $FFFF left or up, 0 none); the list ends with $FF. Tables: location 05 (Underground Castle west) 4 zones, 06 (east) 8, 07 / 08 / 09 (Leo's Paintings 1-3) 2 / 10 / 7, 0B (Leo's Paintings 4) 1, 0C (the Metal Mantis room) 3. The walkthrough calls them conveyor belts ('Work your way across the conveyor belt', 'two carpet-style conveyor belts').

=== BACKGROUND DRIFT ===
Type $07 adds (1, -1) plus scroll_delta_x / scroll_delta_y to its own position every frame and copies the result to the BG2 scroll registers (scroll_bg2_x / y): a slow diagonal drift of the second layer (clouds or a sky). It is placed in the village (A01S01) and in the final scene A00S0D.

=== NOTES ===
- The seven tables carry no names in the ROM; their names come from the location ids the setup actor tests (OQ-I034-6: the map positions were read, not confirmed in the emulator).

gv_title_texts:

TitlePushStartText and TitleCopyrightText are printed by the title actor (gv_obj_title_and_prologue_0066FC in gv_front_end, meta entry $56): the copyright block first, then 'PUSH START' at BG3 offset $4D6 ([09] = two-row glyphs). gv_underground_castle_actors:
The actors of the Underground Castle (area 2) and its shared fairy return prompt (file offsets 107584-111418, bank 03): Lisa in her dream (A02S03), the three fairies of the castle, the elevator (two sprites and a rider) and the colour gradient. The fairies share their setup with the other fairies of the game (shared_actor_helpers_bank3).

=== LISA'S DREAM ===
gv_npc_lisa_dream_01A440 (type $2B, scene A02S03, switch $10 of Lisa) is entered by using the Dream Rod on the sleeping Lisa (gv_village_actors_018000; walkthrough: 'speak with her to enter her dream'). She says 'Daddy, where are you?!'. Lair record $32 (location $0E, tile ($0F,$36), no spawn handler) is the switch of the dream room (walkthrough: 'trigger the switch nearby'): when it is set a voice says 'Lisa, you must tell everything that you know to the person in front of you. They will also need my paintbrush to continue on', Lisa answers 'Daddy! Is that you?' and, talked to again, 'Who are you? Why am I here?' sets flag $0104 and returns the hero to the village (area 1 scene 1, at x $3B0, y $1E0). After the ending (event flag $1F02 set by RunEnding) the same actor runs the epilogue dream: Lisa asks the hero to promise to return someday (a one-answer menu), says 'Thank you. I wish this dream would never end', flag $1F01 is set, scene_variant = 3 and the hero returns to the village at x $3B0, y $1D8, where Lisa starts the ending (gv_village_actors_018000).

=== FAIRIES ===
Three fairies share the return prompt: gv_npc_fairy_exp_30_01AC32 (type $39, A02S01) and gv_npc_fairy_heart_of_castle_01ADF8 (type $5C, A02S02) in this file, and gv_npc_fairy_metal_hint_01AD42 (spawned in the tulip's dream) in gv_leos_paintings_actors. Each talk ends in ReturnToGrassValleyPrompt: 'Would you like to return to Grass Valley?' with the shared Stay / Go back menu; Stay prints 'Come back whenever you feel like returning to Grass Valley'; Go back prints 'Allright, please continue' (the text is as in the ROM, OQ-I034-9), increments contact_lock and warps to the village (area 1 scene 1, x $138, y $3A0). The walkthrough: 'speak with the fairy in the blue gem nearby to return to Grass Valley'.

=== THE ELEVATOR ===
Types $30 / $31 are both placed at tile ($47,$38) in A02S01. Both wait for flag $0404 (the water mill wheel was turned, gv_village_actors_018000); until then the first one says 'I am an elevator invented by Dr-Leo. I cannot move unless the water mill is turning.' when the hero stands on that tile. With the flag set, standing on the lower tile (y $38) and pressing Up plays animation $2A ($2B for the platform), 20 repeats; at the upper tile (y $33) Down plays $2C ($2D). The platform actor ($31, drawn behind) spawns the rider gv_obj_elevator_ride_01AFB9 on each press; the rider locks the input for 81 frames, copies the Y of its spawner to the hero and his weapon and plays a sound every fourth frame (static reading, OQ-I034-6). A hero that is already at x >= $04B0 when the flag is set finds the elevator moved up by $50 pixels.

=== NOTES ===
- Type $2D (gv_fx_hdma_gradient_01B23D) queues gv_hdma_gradient_table_01B24E for register $2132: 127 lines and 32 lines of $E0 (intensity 0), then 16 bands of 4 lines from $E1 to $F0 (intensity 1 to 16).

- The Underground Castle scenes also place the palette-cycle types $02-$05 and $3E (shared palette actors) and, in A02S01-S02, the enemy types $24 / $25 (gv_underground_castle_enemies).

=== THE CLOSING SCENE ===
gv_npc_lisa_epilogue_01B33A (type $5D, tile ($2C,$29)) runs in two passes of area 0 scene $0D. First pass: the screen shows only text (TM = BG3); the Master speaks to the hero: 'My follower, tell me what is on your mind ... being attracted to a human means that you have not yet established yourself as a heavenly creature. A year has now passed, but your feelings have not changed. Maybe you should try living as a human being ... Once you go down to earth you will lose all memory.' Then COP 10 reloads the same scene (arrival animation 2, x $02F0, y $0290 = tile ($2F,$29)); COP 0D finds the hero on that tile and selects the second pass: Lisa speaks to Turbo ('Hey, Turbo, I feel something strange in the air today. What's wrong with me?'), the hero appears in a puff, '<name>? Is that you? Oh, my! I knew you would come back! What is wrong? Don't you remember me?' with a Yes / No menu (Yes, index 0: 'No, I can't believe this' and then the long text; No: the long text only), 'It's okay ... It's me, Lisa, Daughter of Dr-Leo the inventor! ... We can create many new and wonderful memories together!', 'Okay, let me introduce myself. I am Lisa, and the goat behind me is Turbo', 'Come on Turbo, say hello', 'BLEEEET!', 'He looks like a dog I used to have. That is why I call him Turbo. Come, I will show you around.' and 'Hurry up Turbo!'. Lisa then sets event flag $0000 (Turbo moves, gv_npc_turbo_01B967), the pad is overridden to hold Right ($0100) while the hero walks, and after a wait of $014A frames gv_obj_the_end_text_01B508 prints THE END (gv_epilogue_texts) while Lisa's actor ramps coldata_buffer ($E0 | n, n = 0 ... $1F, one step per 2 frames).

=== HOW ONE NPC WORKS ===
The meta types $0B-$18 of MetaGrassValley (WorldMetaPointers) name the twelve roots below, and PlacementA01S01 puts them into the village scene (it also holds the types $19-$1E and $33-$35 of gv_village_actors_019475). The slot of an actor is its row number in the placement list; scripts use it as the slot byte of COP 0C / 0D / 11 / 12 (slot 0 is the hero, slot 4 the old woman, slot 5 the tool shop owner, slot 8 the water mill keeper).
A root is COP 14 ( switch, &appear ) followed by RTL. The switch is the lair record that frees the NPC (data_lair_records: +9 is the name index into NpcNameStrings, +2 / +3 the home tile, +B the lair location; the walkthrough chapter 2 lists the lairs). While the switch bit in $1ADE is clear the actor stays hidden ($16 bit $2000 from the placement) and only waits; once the lair is released COP 14 clears the bit and jumps to the appear handler. That handler spawns the appear puff (engine_spawn_lairs_death_drops.RunAppearPuff), registers the talk handler with COP 17 (the word goes to $30; the engine runs it when the hero talks to the actor) and blocks the actor's tiles with COP 15. A talk handler picks its string with event flags (COP 07 / COP 09) or the inventory (COP 18 / COP 19 test an item entry) and ends with RTL. COP 30 ( record, &child, #03 ) spawns a one-shot text actor when the hero enters the scene on the return trip after freeing that NPC. Most strings end with [JMP shared_actor_helpers_bank3.asciistring_01B988], the dialogue box erase.

lib_animation:
Record stepper used by the animation COP commands Cop92-Cop95 (file offsets 67163-67312, SNES $02:865B-$86F0, bank 02).

=== MODEL ===
An actor field set drives a list of 6-byte records: $1E = animation id, $20 = step, $24 = data bank. The word list at $8000 of that bank (one word per animation id) points to the records. NextFrameRecord loads the record of the current step into the actor's work fields; CopyFrameData copies the bytes the record points to into WRAM bank $7F.
Record (6 bytes): +0 duration (0 = end of the animation), +1 word source address (bank $24,X) -> $08,X, +3 byte x 2 -> $0A,X (destination offset), +4 byte -> $0C,X (byte count - 1 for the block move), +5 byte -> $0E,X and $14,X (the wait reload). The tick counter $26,X = duration - 1.
The destination is bank $7F offset $0A,X, i.e. the CGRAM shadow $7F0000 (two bytes per colour) when the offset is a colour index x 2; a count byte of 2 (three bytes) adds $200 to the offset, which lands on coldata_buffer ($7F0200, the three COLDATA bytes). This makes the stepper a colour animation, but nothing in the code names it, so it is inferred from the destination (OQ-I026-3).

=== NOTES ===
- The block move runs through a RAM stub at $1C5C built by the scene init (lib_boot_and_scene_init): PHB, MVN, PLB, RTS. CopyFrameData patches its two bank operands (wram_copy_stub+2): destination $7F, source = the actor's data bank.
lib_arithmetic:
Hardware multiply and divide wrappers and packed BCD (file offsets 78289-78333 and 78357-78405, SNES $02:B1D1-$B1FD and $02:B215-$B245, bank 02; the neighbours SignExtendByte, ArithmeticShiftRight and StepRandomState at 78334-78349, 78350-78356 and 78406-78449 have part notes of their own).

=== MODEL ===
Multiply8x8 and DivideWordByByte use the SNES multiplier ($4202/$4203) and divider ($4204-$4206): write the operands, wait the fixed time with NOPs and read the result. All three routines are entered by long call with M = 8 and X = 16 and have no side effects beyond A, B and the hardware registers. ByteToPackedBcd converts 0-255 to the packed BCD that the text control [06:n,addr] prints (digit bytes, least significant first).

=== NOTES ===
- Multiply8x8 has about 22 call sites (map streaming and sweep, scene loading, COP core, combat and spawn code, ChooseFacingAnim); DivideWordByByte only two: ChooseFacingAnim and shared_actor_helpers_bank0.

Choice menus of bank 02: the row chooser, the question window chooser and the cursor blink they share (file offsets 74040-74537, SNES $02:A138-$A329).

One file because ChooseMenuRow (with ChooseMenuRowAtTable and TitleMenuCursorOffsets) and RunChoiceMenu both blink their cursor through BlinkChoiceCursor, which nothing else calls. Callers: lib_menus (ChooseMenuRow), engine_title_file_select (ChooseMenuRowAtTable, the file select) and cop_items_stats_text (RunChoiceMenu, the question windows of Cop1A_ChoiceMenu). The sections below keep the notes of the former files in file order.

Menu row chooser (file offsets 74040-74368, SNES $02:A138-$A280, bank 02; the cursor offset table is at 74359-74368).

=== MODEL ===
A cursor of one glyph (BG3 tile $2B, drawn in the cell at the row's offset and in the cell one tilemap row above it) moves between a few rows of a menu. ChooseMenuRow serves the equipment menu: rows are $80 apart in the BG3 buffer (two text rows), Up and Down move, Y cancels (carry set) and B confirms (carry clear); the equipment menu uses it with four rows (Weapon, Armor, Magic, Item) and swaps the page on the way. ChooseMenuRowAtTable is the same loop for the file-select and erase menus of engine_title_file_select: the row offsets come from TitleMenuCursorOffsets ($C0 apart) and there is no page swap; B plays the confirm sound ($18) there and the cancel and move sounds are $07 (OQ-I009-12).
Both wait for all buttons to be up (lib_text_render.WaitFrameReadButtons, which returns the high byte of joy_pressed) before reading a press and call lib_choice_menus.BlinkChoiceCursor while waiting (it blinks the cursor glyph; menu_blink counts the frames).

=== NOTES ===
- Input: A = row count (stored in menu_count), B (after XBA) = start row, X = BG3 byte offset of the start row's cursor cell. Output: carry clear and A = row; carry set when Y was pressed. The final cursor glyph stays drawn on the last row.
- The first 'wait until released' loop gives an edge-triggered feel: joy_pressed holds a button as long as it is down (or until the latch is cleared), so a held button would otherwise repeat.

Choice menu: the arrow cursor list of every question window (file offsets 74369-74506, SNES $02:A281-$A30A, bank 02).

=== MODEL ===
RunChoiceMenu is called by Cop1A_ChoiceMenu (27 scripts) and Cop02_PromptYesNo (no script uses it) after the option window of shared_choice_prompt_texts has been printed. A = number of options (8 bit), the high byte of A (read with XBA) = the start index (both callers pass 0), X = BG3 byte offset of the first option's arrow cell. Options are $80 bytes apart (two tile rows). The selected index is kept on the stack ($01,S) for the whole menu; menu_count ($03C4) holds the option count and menu_blink ($03C6) the blink frame counter.
The arrow is the glyph tile $2B, two tiles tall like every glyph: the lower half at X in the BG3 buffer ($7F7000) and the upper half one row above (X - $40, the buffer base $7F6FC0 + X). Only the tile byte is written, the attribute stays. Blank is tile $20.
Flow: (1) DrawChoiceCursor writes the arrow and sets vram_upload_flags bit 0. (2) WaitChoiceKeysUp calls WaitFrameReadButtons and BlinkChoiceCursor until a frame reports no new button press, so the press that opened the question cannot answer it. (3) PollChoiceKeys reads one frame at a time (joy_pressed+1: $08 Up, $04 Down, $40 Y, $80 B); any other frame runs BlinkChoiceCursor and polls again. Up on the first option and Down on the last go back to step 2 (the move is ignored). A move erases the arrow (tile $20 in both halves), plays BRK #$07, resets menu_blink, moves the cell by $80 and redraws.
Exit: B plays BRK #$18 and returns carry clear, Y plays BRK #$07 and returns carry set. In both cases the arrow stays drawn (tile $2B) on the current option, A = the index pulled off the stack and X = its arrow cell. The callers then erase the window (EraseWindowFrame at text_last_window_origin, $03F7), set vram_upload_flags = 1 and either store the index in choice_result ($03D0) or, on cancel, take the cancel pointer.

=== NOTES ===
- B = confirm and Y = cancel match the walkthrough ('Press the B Button twice to equip ... Press the Y Button to exit the menu', 01-in-the-beginning.md). The other buttons are ignored here.
- ChooseMenuRow and ChooseMenuRowAtTable (lib_choice_menus) are the same loop for the equipment, file-select and erase menus with their own row spacing and page swap; they share BlinkChoiceCursor with this routine.
- Nothing limits the option count except the window: the largest in use is 3.

lib_field_talk:
Field talk: the B-button interaction that starts the script of an NPC in front of the player (file offsets 72152-72598, SNES $02:99D8-$9B96, bank 02).

=== MODEL ===
RunTalkInteraction (B) disables NMI, runs FindAndTalkToActorInFront and enables NMI: the script drives its own frames. The probe point depends on the facing code (from lib_player_helpers.GetPlayerFacing): code 0 (x+8, y-$10), 1 (x+8, y), 2 (x+$10, y-8), 3 (x, y-8) relative to the player's (x, y); facing 0 probes a second point two tiles up when the tile type there is 6. FindTalkableActorAt walks the actors from actor_list_tail through the $3E links and accepts the first one whose $16 has bit $0040 and whose box contains the point (x is the left edge, y the bottom edge, $10 and $12 width and height). ActivateTalkTarget needs $30,X (the script address, stored by Cop17_SetOwnParam, for example the first actor of gv_village_actors_018000) and calls it through an RTL frame: pushed bank $02 and ReturnFromTalk - 1, then the script bank (byte +$D of the actor's meta entry at $38,X) and $30,X - 1. With $16 bit $0008 the NPC first turns to face the player: TalkFacingPlayer copies the whole slot ($40 bytes) to $1A1E, ChooseFacingAnim picks the animation, the script runs, RestoreTalkedActor copies the slot back. So $16 bit $0040 = talkable and bit $0008 = turn to face the player (OQ-I005-14, OQ-I009-17).

=== NOTES ===
- The only entry is RunTalkInteraction: DispatchFieldButtons (lib_menus) branches to it with one BRL when B is pressed. GetPlayerFacing and FlipActorX come from lib_player_helpers. The parts are RunTalkInteraction, FindAndTalkToActorInFront, FindTalkableActorAt (with the sub-labels ActivateTalkTarget and TalkFacingPlayer), RestoreTalkedActor, ReturnFromTalk and ChooseFacingAnim.
lib_hdma_window_effects:
HDMA effects of the main loop and the four Soul window effects (file offsets 71317-71773, SNES $02:9695-$985D, bank 02).

=== BG3 SCROLL HDMA ===
QueueBg3ScrollHdma is called at the end of each of the five sub-frame runners of the main loop (engine_boot_main_loop). In every location except $10-$12 (location_id - $10 below 3) it queues Bg3ScrollHdmaTable for PPU register $12 (BG3VOFS, a byte written twice per line) on the next free HDMA channel (lib_system_helpers.QueueHdmaDirect). The table covers 48 lines: scroll offset -4 for 20 lines, 0 for 12, +4 for 12, then +3, +2, +1 and 0 for one line each. HDMA has to be queued again every frame (ResetHdmaQueue empties the queue at the start of each work phase), which is why the call repeats. What the table is for is open (OQ-I042-1).

=== SOUL WINDOW EFFECTS ===
RunSoulOfLightEffect, RunSoulOfRealityEffect, RunSoulOfDetectionEffect and RunSoulOfShieldEffect are actor scripts: each is the script address of meta entries of WorldMetaPointers (flags $2010, EffectAnims). Each tests its bit in souls_flags ($1B82: $02 Light, $10 Reality, $08 Detection, $04 Shield, see docs/wram-memory-map.md and OQ-I006-10) and returns at once while the soul is not recruited, so the actor polls every frame. Once the bit is set it writes the window and colour-math registers of its soul one time:
- Light ($02): W12SEL = 0, W34SEL = 0, WOBJSEL = $30, CGWSEL = $12.
- Reality ($10): W12SEL = $20 (and its shadow w12sel_shadow), W34SEL = 0, WOBJSEL = 0, bg2_offset_x and bg2_offset_y = 1.
- Detection ($08): W12SEL = $20 (and the shadow), W34SEL = 0, WOBJSEL = 1, bg2_offset_x and bg2_offset_y = 1.
- Shield ($04): W12SEL = $33 (and the shadow), W34SEL = 0, WOBJSEL = 0, TMW = 0, TSW = 3, CGWSEL = $82, and it spawns the Soul of Shield sweep (COP B0, engine_player_death_and_actor_helpers.DestroyHazardsNearOrb).
All four then fall into BuildSoulOrbCircleWindow. Its first command is COP 91 (Cop91_SetEntryHere), so from the next frame on the actor runs only the circle rebuild.

=== THE CIRCLE ===
BuildSoulOrbCircleWindow takes the soul orb actor (soul_orb_actor, $03A0) and turns its position into screen coordinates (x - scroll_bg1_x + 8 clamped to 0-$FF, y - scroll_bg1_y - 8 clamped to 0-$DF). It writes two HDMA tables to $7E:7000 and $7E:7800: for each pair of scanlines the left and right edge of window 1 from data_engine_tables.CircleHalfWidths (a circle of radius $40 pixels around the orb), clipped to the screen, closed by one line with both edges $FF (WH0 = WH1 = $FF, a window one pixel wide at x = 255, OQ-I051-3) and a zero terminator. Both tables are queued for PPU registers $26 (WH0) and $27 (WH1). What each soul does with that window (which layers it clips) is not decoded here (OQ-I042-2).

=== NOTES ===
- The extraction has no reference to the four entries from code; they are reached through the meta entries of WorldMetaPointers (the 4 table references).
lib_hud:
HUD update, enemy gauge and the HUD strings (UpdateHud at file offsets 75353-75470, SNES $02:A659-$A6CE; HudRepeatCounts and HudFrameText with the enemy gauge strings at 83724-83848, SNES $02:C70C-$C788; bank 02). UpdateHud is the only reader of the strings, so they live in this file.

=== MODEL ===
UpdateHud runs once per frame at the end of the work phase (RunMainLoop step 7, RunReturnLoop, RunSubFrame) and once from ShowStatusAndSoulsScreen. It draws the enemy gauge, pays out the pending heal and EXP (lib_player_helpers.DrainPendingHeal and DrainPendingExp) and redraws the parts of the HUD that hud_dirty_flags marks.
Locations $0F-$12 have no HUD: UpdateHud returns at once for location_id - $0F below 4, so the heal and EXP drains and the redraw are skipped there too, and the dirty bits are cleared (FM-A5 section 1.8 said the drains still ran; the code does not). The reduced loop of $10-$12 never calls it; location $0F still runs the full main loop (OQ-I027-2).

=== ENEMY GAUGE ===
enemy_gauge_timer ($0330) is one byte. A hit sets it to $80 (SetEnemyGauge in engine_combat_hits); on the next UpdateHud $80 is the only value that draws the gauge (EnemyGaugeText: a fixed six-tile label, entry 1 of the text renderer's list TextListPointers, and the bar from enemy_gauge_hp and enemy_gauge_max). The timer then counts down by 2 per frame ($7E ... $00, 63 frames, about one second); at 0 the clear string is drawn and the timer becomes $FE; every other negative value is idle and draws nothing (OQ-I009-15).

=== HUD PARTS ===
hud_dirty_flags ($0332) is shifted out bit by bit: bit 0 HudFrameText (the backing tiles, the LEV, EXP and GEM labels and a fixed six-tile label, entry 0 of TextListPointers), bit 1 HudExpText (8 BCD digits from player_exp), bit 2 HudHpGaugeText (the HP gauge from player_hp and player_max_hp), bit 3 HudLevelText (2 digits from player_level_bcd's low byte at $1B6A), bit 4 HudGemsText (6 digits from gems_low). The menus store $1F to redraw everything; hits set bits 1 and 2, pickups bit 4.

=== NOTES ===
- The BG3 cells are written into the buffer by the text renderer (lib_text_render.PrintTextString) and reach VRAM through the upload flags it sets.

lib_map_scroll_and_redraw:
Camera aim, scroll streaming and the sweep redraw: everything that keeps the BG1 and BG2 maps on screen (file offsets 65536-67162 and 69354-69929, SNES $02:8000-$865A and $02:8EEA-$9129; SweepStepTable at 93741-94860; bank 02).

One file because the main loop, the NMI and the scene init call all three parts and the parts need nothing but lib_arithmetic. The sections below keep the notes of the three routines in file order: the camera aim, the scroll streaming, the sweep redraw.

Camera aim: one routine, AimCameraAtPlayer (file offsets 65536-65640, SNES $02:8000-$8068, bank 02).

The camera follows the player without smoothing: AimCameraAtPlayer converts 'where the camera should be' into the signed deltas scroll_delta_x and scroll_delta_y, and ScrollCameraByDelta (lib_map_scroll_and_redraw) applies them in the same frame. The whole scroll model is in the lib_map_scroll_and_redraw block note.

Scroll streaming: camera update, strip building and strip upload (file offsets 65641-67162, SNES $02:8069-$865A, bank 02).

=== SCREEN MODEL ===
BG1 and BG2 each show a map that is larger than their VRAM tilemap (64 x 64 tiles = 512 x 512 pixels). A map is a grid of 16 x 16 pixel metatiles stored one byte per metatile at $7E8000 (BG1) and $7EC000 (BG2), in pages of 256 bytes (16 x 16 metatiles = 256 x 256 pixels): page = (y >> 8) x map_width_pages + (x >> 8), cell = ((y >> 4) and 15) x 16 + ((x >> 4) and 15). map_width_px ($0342, word) is map_width_pages x 256; map_height_px likewise. A metatile definition is 8 bytes (four tile words: top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right) at $7E2000 (BG1) and $7E2800 (BG2). Bit 9 of a tile word is not a tile bit: it is the solid flag of that quarter, the mask $FDFF removes it before the word reaches VRAM, and SetMetatileBg1 gathers the four flags into the low nibble of the tile_type_map byte ($7F8000).
The per-layer tables are word pairs indexed by X = 0 (BG1) or X = 4 (BG2): scroll_bg1_x/y and scroll_bg2_x/y, map_width_px/map_height_px, the parallax ratios ratio_x_bg1 .. ratio_y_bg2, map_base_bg1/2 ($8000, $C000), tilemap_vram_bg1/2 ($6000, $7000), tile_defs_bg1/2, tile_mask_bg1/2, tile_attr_bg1/2 and the strip buffers strip_col_bg1 .. strip_row_bg2. The scene loader fills them (lib_boot_and_scene_init, lib_scene_asset_loader).

=== ONE FRAME ===
Work phase (NMI off): AimCameraAtPlayer stores scroll_delta_x/y; ScrollCameraByDelta adds them to scroll_bg1_x/y (clamped to the map), derives BG2 from BG1 through the ratios (UpdateLayerScrollX/Y) and sets a request bit in scroll_requests ($0396: $80 = BG1 column, $40 = BG1 row, $20 = BG2 column, $10 = BG2 row) whenever the scroll crosses a 16-pixel line (bit 4 of the position changed); BuildScrollStrips tests and clears each bit and builds the strip for it (BuildColumnStrip / BuildRowStrip), then zeroes scroll_delta_x/y. In the NMI, UploadMapStripBuffers calls UploadScrollStrips for the BG1 pair and the BG2 pair of buffers.
A strip record is 258 bytes in bank $7E: a word (the VRAM address of the strip, 0 = empty) and four blocks of 64 bytes. A column strip is one metatile column of the whole tilemap height: 2 tile columns x 64 tiles, written with VMAIN $81 (increment 32 words); a row strip is one metatile row of the whole width: 2 tile rows x 64 tiles, written with VMAIN $80. The blocks go to the VRAM address, address + 1 (or + $20), + $800 (or + $400) and + $801 (or + $420): the four 32 x 32 tile screens of a 64 x 64 tilemap. Buffer addresses: BG1 column $3000, BG1 row $3102, BG2 column $3204, BG2 row $3306.
A column strip goes at the right edge of the view (scroll x + $100) for a positive delta and at the left edge (scroll x) for a negative one; a row strip likewise below (scroll y + $100) or above. FillColumnStripBuffer / FillRowStripBuffer read 2 pages along the strip (the second is the next page, wrapping at the end of the map for columns) and CopyMetatileColumn / CopyMetatileRow expand 16 metatiles into 2 x 2 tiles each, applying the layer's tile mask and attribute.

=== ENTRY REDRAW ===
RedrawBackgroundsAtEntry (called once by the scene change code, not for location $10) places the camera on the player, derives BG2, wraps the BG2 scroll into its map and then builds and uploads 32 column strips per layer (32 x 16 px = the whole 512-pixel tilemap width), one strip at a time through UploadScrollStrips with NMI off.

=== NOTES ===
- ScaleByRatio computes scroll x numerator / divisor: the ratio word has the numerator in its low byte and the divisor in its high byte (using the PPU multiplier $211B/$211C and the hardware divider $4204/$4206), so $0201 is half speed and $0101 is the same speed.
- BuildScrollStrips is mis-decoded by the extractor (OQ-I005-7, OQ-I026-1): read its part note for the real code.
- scroll_bg1_x/y and scroll_bg2_x/y are positions in map pixels; the NMI writes them to the PPU scroll registers (WriteScrollRegisters; bg_scroll_swap exchanges the two pairs between BG1 and BG2).

Sweep redraw: redraws the visible map line by line from the map data (code at file offsets 69354-69929, SNES $02:8EEA-$9129; SweepStepTable 93741-94860, SNES $02:EE2D-$F28C; bank 02).

=== MODEL ===
After a map rectangle was copied (lair release, plate, NPC release scenes) the screen still shows the old tiles. The sweep step counter sweep_step ($1C75, a word) walks from 1 to 35; StepSweepRedraw is called once per frame by RunSubFrameMapSweep and, while sweep_step is non-zero, redraws one line of 16 metatiles of the 17 x 17 view (the visible map area measured from the 16-pixel aligned scroll origin sweep_origin_x/y) into vram_write_queue. The order is in SweepStepTable: columns and rows alternate outwards from the middle (column 7, row 7, column 8, row 8, column 6, row 6, ...), the last steps cover the 17th column and row because the scroll is not aligned to 16 pixels. sweep_bg1 chooses the layer: non-zero = BG1 (tilemap $6000, map $7E8000, definitions $7E2000), zero = BG2 (tilemap $7000, map $7EC000, definitions $7E2800). After step 35 the counter returns to 0 (idle).
The callers start a sweep with sweep_step = 1 and sweep_bg1 = 1 and then call RunSubFrameMapSweep 35 times; a two-layer release does a BG2 sweep first (sweep_bg1 = 0) and a BG1 sweep after it.

=== NOTES ===
- SweepStepTable: 35 steps x 32 bytes: 16 x indexes (0-$10) then 16 y indexes. Even steps are columns (x constant, y = 0-$F), odd steps rows.
lib_map_tile_patches:
Run-time and scene-load changes of the metatile maps (code at file offsets 67313-68053 and 69930-71316, SNES $02:86F1-$89D5 and $02:912A-$9694; tables at 94861-95787; bank 02).

One file because all of it writes the BG1 and BG2 metatile maps or the tile type map, uses lib_map_index_helpers (30 lines of the file mention it) and is driven by the same data tables (data_lair_records, data_plate_lists, data_chest_lists, data_exit_lists, FlagMapPatchTable). The parts are: SetMetatileBg1 and SetMetatileBg1Bg2 (one metatile), ApplyMapPatchRect, CopyMapRectFromSlab, CopyMapRectFromStaging and CopyMapRectFromStagingBothLayers (rectangle copies), the scene-load patches that InitSceneState runs (SetHeldLairTileType, ApplyReleasedLairRects, ApplyLairStatesToScene, InitPlateVariantAtEntry, InitExitListOffset, ShowOpenedChests, ApplyFlagMapPatches) and the two tables FlagMapPatchTable and MapPatchRectsAndMapSizes. The sections below keep the notes of the three former files.

Metatile writers: put one metatile into the map and, when it is on screen, queue it for VRAM (file offsets 67313-67770, SNES $02:86F1-$88BA, bank 02).

=== MODEL ===
Both routines (1) turn the pixel position in dp$16 / $18 into a map offset (lib_map_index_helpers.PixelToMapIndex), (2) store the metatile id in the BG1 map ($7E8000) and, for SetMetatileBg1Bg2, also in the BG2 map ($7EC000), (3) rewrite the tile_type_map byte ($7F8000) from the definition (the solid flag, bit 9, of the four tile words gives bits 0 to 3: top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right) and (4) when the metatile lies in the view plus 16 pixels, write four (VRAM address, tile word) entries per layer to vram_write_queue ($1C7B, 4 bytes per entry, 16 per metatile) and a zero terminator; the NMI (FlushVramWriteQueue) draws them.
The queue is overwritten from its start: callers either wait for it to be empty first (SealLair) or call right after the NMI has emptied it (the tile triggers).
Callers: SealLair (green switch $FE), CheckPlayerTileTriggers / TryOpenChest (open chest $FC) and ReleaseLairAtSwitch's own map write (it writes the map bytes directly).

Map patch rectangles: copy a rectangle of the map to another place, and the table that holds the five boss-room patches followed by the map sizes (ApplyMapPatchRect: file offsets 67771-68053, SNES $02:88BB-$89D5; MapPatchRectsAndMapSizes: 95492-95787, SNES $02:F504-$F62B; bank 02).

=== MODEL ===
ApplyMapPatchRect copies a rectangle of metatiles (and their tile_type_map bytes) inside the BG1 map: from the source rectangle given in the record's pixel words +4 / +6 to the destination given by +0 / +1 (metatile units), width +2, height +3; then every copied cell that is on screen is queued for VRAM (16 bytes per cell in vram_write_queue, zero terminator). It is the boss-room patch: RunBossMapPatch (engine_player_death_and_actor_helpers) calls it with the id 0-4 stored by five boss scripts (whether the patch closes or opens the room is OQ-I024-3).

=== TABLE ===
MapPatchRectsAndMapSizes holds two tables back to back in one 296-byte part: 5 patch records of 8 bytes (entries 00-04 of the extracted rows) and, from byte $28, 128 pairs (map_width_pages, map_height_pages) indexed by location_id x 2, read by lib_boot_and_scene_init (OQ-I026-2: the part should be split in blocks.json).
Patch record: +0 destination x, +1 destination y (metatiles), +2 width, +3 height (metatiles), +4 word source x, +6 word source y (pixels).

Map rectangle copies of the release scenes (file offsets 69930-70388, SNES $02:912A-$92F4, bank 02), the five scene-load patches ApplyReleasedLairRects, SetHeldLairTileType, InitPlateVariantAtEntry, InitExitListOffset and ShowOpenedChests (70389-71037), the lair state and flag map patches that run at every scene load (ApplyLairStatesToScene 71038-71152, ApplyFlagMapPatches 71153-71265, LookupSceneVariant 71266-71316, SNES $02:957E-$96D4) and FlagMapPatchTable (94861-95491, SNES $02:F28D-$F503).

=== MODEL: RELEASE SCENES ===
The rectangle is given by the copied lair record bytes in $1C6D-$1C74: release_slab ($1C6E), release_npc_x/y ($1C6F-$1C70), release_rect_x/y ($1C71-$1C72, the destination in metatiles) and release_rect_w/h ($1C73-$1C74). A slab is an alternative full-size copy of the map stored behind the live map in the $7E8000 region: slab k starts k x (map size in bytes) after the live map; its cells are copied onto the same cells of the live map (CopyMapRectFromSlab). The staging copies instead read from a rectangle of the live map itself whose position the caller put in dp$16 / $18 (record +E / +F) and write to release_rect_x/y.
CopyMapRectFromSlab keeps the high nibble of the live collision byte (the actor block bits $F0) and takes the low nibble from the slab; the staging copies replace the whole byte. A width or height of $80 or more would hang on a BCS to itself (the guard before the loops); the shipped records never do that.
Nothing is queued for VRAM by these routines: the sweep redraw (StepSweepRedraw) draws the result.

=== MODEL: SCENE LOAD ===
InitSceneState (lib_boot_and_scene_init) calls ApplyLairStatesToScene and ApplyFlagMapPatches right after LoadSceneAssets, so the map pages and collision map they change are the ones just loaded. The two routines make the scene show what the player already did: lairs that are released stay open and gone, and rooms whose event flag is set show their opened state.
ApplyLairStatesToScene visits the 420 lair records of LairRecords (32 bytes each, $FF terminator) with a running index X over ALL records (lair_state[X] is the state byte of record X). Records of this location count in lairs_left (the number the pause banner shows). State above 0: the lair still has monsters, SpawnLairActor creates it. State 0: every monster is dead and the tile at the record's (+C, +D) becomes $FE (the lair's release switch). State below 0: the lair was released, the tile becomes $FF and the lair stops counting. The tile is written to the BG1 page $7E8000 and, when record +8 is non-zero, to the BG2 page $7EC000.
ApplyFlagMapPatches walks FlagMapPatchTable. For each row of this location whose event flag is set it copies a rectangle of the map from a hidden staging place of the same map to the visible place (CopyMapRectFromStaging): the permanent map changes of the game (opened doors and passages). LookupSceneVariant walks SceneVariantRules and is called from ApplySceneProfile (see lib_scene_asset_loader).

=== NOTES ===
- ApplyReleasedLairRects, SetHeldLairTileType (with the sub-label InitPlateVariantAtEntry), InitExitListOffset and ShowOpenedChests are read from the code only; no scene was traced with them at run time (OQ-I042-4). InitSceneState calls them in the order SetHeldLairTileType, ApplyReleasedLairRects, ApplyLairStatesToScene, InitPlateVariantAtEntry, InitExitListOffset, ShowOpenedChests, ApplyFlagMapPatches.
- 13 of the 70 FlagMapPatchTable rows test event flag number $00FF (locations 00, 0E, 13, 71, 72, 73). It is bit 7 of $1A7D, set at every start-up by InitFixedState and never cleared, so these 13 rows always apply.

Menu screen setup of bank 02: the BG2 menu screen (SetupMenuBg2Screen), the menu tile groups (ExpandMenuTileGroups), the menu graphics and palette loaders, the item page palette, the scene graphics restore and the equipped magic graphics (file offsets 74539-74575, 74640-74989 and the loaders up to the end of the file, SNES $02:A32B-$A34F and $02:A390-$A4ED).

One file because SetupMenuBg2Screen calls LoadMenuBg2Graphics, LoadMenuPalette and ExpandMenuTileGroups together, and the other parts load or restore the graphics and palettes that a menu replaces. Callers: engine_title_file_select (SetupMenuBg2Screen), lib_menus (LoadMenuBg2Graphics, LoadMenuPalette, LoadItemPagePalette, RestoreSceneBgGfxAndPalette, LoadEquippedMagicGfx), lib_boot_and_scene_init (RestoreSceneBgGfxAndPalette, LoadEquippedMagicGfx) and gv_front_end (RestoreSceneBgGfxAndPalette). The sections below keep the notes of the loaders; SetupMenuBg2Screen and ExpandMenuTileGroups have part notes.

Menu graphics and palette loaders (file offsets 74774-74832, SNES $02:A416-$A44F, bank 02).

=== MODEL ===
Two short routines give the field menus and the file-select screen their own BG2 tile set and colours. LoadMenuBg2Graphics DMAs graphics_04B000 ($09:B000, 8192 bytes, 256 4bpp tiles) to VRAM word $2000; LoadMenuPalette copies 256 bytes of data_menu_palettes_and_groups.MenuBgPalette ($09:F100) into the CGRAM buffer (cgram_buffer, colours 0-127), which the NMI uploads.

Both are called in this order by OpenEquipmentMenu (lib_menus) and by lib_menu_screen_setup (the setup of the file-select screen, called from EnterFileSelect). RedrawEquipmentPage (lib_menus) calls LoadMenuPalette alone to bring the equipment palette back after the item page.

=== NOTES ===
- VRAM word $2000 is the BG2 character base: lib_menu_screen_setup writes BG12NBA = $20, BG2SC = $5C and BGMODE = 9 right before it calls these routines, and OpenEquipmentMenu writes the same BG2SC and BG12NBA. That graphics_04B000 is the menu icon and frame set and MenuBgPalette its palette is a reading of the callers (OQ-I010-10).
- LoadMenuBg2Graphics does not write VMAIN ($2115); it relies on a value left by earlier code (OQ-I010-8) and on forced blank (both callers blank the screen first).
- The wrapper docs earlier called these code_012416 and code_01243D and the first one a '4 KB' set; the DMA size is $2000 bytes (8 KB, 4K words).

Palette and graphics handoff of the menus (file offsets 74832-74989, SNES $02:A450-$A4ED, bank 02).

=== MODEL ===
The equipment menu replaces the field's VRAM character data at word $2000 with its own graphics and the palette with its own, and puts the field back on exit. LoadItemPagePalette gives the item page its palette (colours 0-127 from ItemPagePalette). RestoreSceneBgGfxAndPalette DMAs the 8 KB copy of graphics_04D000 that lib_boot_and_scene_init keeps at $7F:C000 back to VRAM word $2000 and restores palettes 11-15 (MenuSpellPalettes, 160 bytes, to cgram_buffer + $160); the scene change (lib_boot_and_scene_init, when $0454 is set) and code_0066DE of gv_front_end call it too. LoadEquippedMagicGfx then puts the graphics and palette of the equipped spell on top.
On the menu exit the order is RestoreSceneBgGfxAndPalette, RestoreCgramBuffer (which overwrites the whole CGRAM buffer, including the colours just written) and LoadEquippedMagicGfx: the spell palette is loaded last so it survives.

=== NOTES ===
- What graphics_04D000 is (field BG or shared tile set): OQ-I009-13.
- Spell n = equipped_magic - $11 (0-7). MagicGraphicsPointers holds a 3-byte pointer per spell (graphics_07B000 plus $0, $0, $800, $1000, $1000, $1800, $1800, $800), MagicPalettePointers also a 3-byte pointer per spell (palette_07D000 + $20 x n; LoadEquippedMagicGfx indexes both tables with 3 x n and reads only the word of the palette entry, the source bank is fixed to $0F).
lib_menus:
Field menus and screens (status and souls, equipment and item menu), their menu text and the item descriptions (code at file offsets 71932-72151 and 72599-73976, SNES $02:98FC-$99D7 and $02:9B97-$A0F8, plus helpers at 74576-74639 and 74730-74773; text and tables at 83313-83723, 85876-86757 (ItemNameList and the item names) and 87358-90589; bank 02). The talk routines (72152-72598) are in lib_field_talk, the HUD strings in lib_hud and EnableDisplayAndNmi in lib_system_helpers.

=== FIELD BUTTONS ===
DispatchFieldButtons runs once per frame from RunMainLoop with NMI on (M = 8). Order: Select or X (joy_pressed+1 bit $20; the NMI copies X into the Select bit) opens the equipment menu; B ($80) talks to the actor in front of the player; A (low byte of joy_pressed, bit 7), only when no direction is held, shows the status and souls screen. Walkthrough 01-in-the-beginning.md: 'Press the X Button to open the menu ... Press the B Button twice to equip ... Press the Y Button to exit the menu', 'speak with him (B Button)'. The A-button screen is not in the walkthrough (OQ-I009-5). joy_pressed keeps a button as long as its release latch bit is set (engine_vblank_nmi JOYPAD note), so every chooser first waits until all buttons are up and the screens that end on a button clear the latch bits with TRB, to stop the same press acting in the field.

=== STATUS AND SOULS SCREEN ===
A BG3-only overlay (no screen blank, no graphics swap). ShowStatusAndSoulsScreen converts HP and maximum HP to BCD (hp_bcd, max_hp_bcd), clamps the strength and defence level parts (level_power, level_defense) to 12 for the display and restores them afterwards (OQ-I009-6), and prints StatusScreenText: the player name, HP / maximum, the EXP total of the next level (player_exp_next: the LevelExpThresholds value that WatchForLevelUp compares with player_exp, not a remainder; 8 digits), bars for Strength and Defence (two rows each, level part over gear part) and the four equipped item names. After A is released it waits for A, B, Y or a direction, prints the souls page (SoulsScreenTitleText, then one 21-byte line per bit of souls_flags: bit 0 Magician, 1 Light, 2 Shield, 3 Detection, 4 Reality), waits for release and another press, consumes the latch and clears BG3. WaitFrameKeepClock undoes the NMI's frame_counter increment, so the frame clock stands still while the screen is open.

=== INVENTORY TABLE AND SLOT BYTE ===
inventory ($1B1E) is one 64-byte table indexed by item id minus 1. The four lists of the menu are ranges of it: weapons ids $01-$08 (8 slots, $1B1E), armors $09-$10 ($1B26), magic $11-$18 ($1B2E) and items $19-$40 (40 slots, $1B36; walkthrough grid position (row, column) is slot (row - 1) x 10 + column - 1). A slot byte holds the item id in bits 0-6 (0 = not owned; an owned slot holds the id of its own slot) and bit 7 = marker: the equipped item of each list, and during a choice the cursor. DrawInventoryIcon draws a selection frame around every slot with bit 7. The equipped state is stored twice: the marker in the list and the id in the word cells equipped_weapon, equipped_armor, equipped_magic and equipped_bracelet (high bytes never written; the text codes read them as words).
Choosing from a list (ChooseFromEquipmentList, ChooseItemSlot): the cursor starts on the first slot with bit 7 set, or marks slot 0 when none is; the list is backed up to $7F0403 (only the dead cancel paths restore it); a direction moves the marker and resets menu_blink; B and Y both confirm (BRK #$18), set the marker on the slot and return A = id with carry clear. No live path cancels (CancelEquipChoice and CancelItemChoice are unreferenced, OQ-I009-14), so choosing an empty slot returns 0, which the caller stores in the equipped cell: name index 0 is the string 'not equipped'. Weapons, armors and magic are two columns of four, column-major (Right +4, Left -4, Down +1, Up -1); items are four rows of ten, row-major (Right +1, Left -1, Down +10, Up -10). A step past an end leaves the cursor where it is; stepping down from the last slot of a column goes to the top of the next.

=== EQUIPMENT MENU ===
OpenEquipmentMenu (X or Select): HDMA off (dp$42 = 0), forced blank, BG2 map at VRAM $5C00 and characters at $2000, main screen BG2 and BG3 only, colour math and windows off; saves the four scroll words (menu_saved_bg1_x .. menu_saved_bg2_y) and zeroes the live ones, saves the CGRAM buffer ($7E6000), loads the menu graphics, palette and tile groups (LoadMenuBg2Graphics, LoadMenuPalette, ExpandMenuTileGroups in lib_menu_screen_setup), runs RunEquipmentMenu. RunEquipmentMenu prints EquipMenuFrameText (tabs Weapon, Armor, Magic at $88, $98, $A8, the description window at $408 and four equipped-item lines), switches NMI and the screen on, draws the icons, uploads the BG3 page and then the BG2 icon page ($7F7800 to VRAM $5C00), and loops on ChooseMenuRow: rows 0-2 call ChooseFromEquipmentList (A = 8, Y = list base), row 3 ChooseItemSlot (A = $28, Y = $1B36). A confirmed id is stored in the equipped cell (weapon and armor then RecalcGearStats) and the frame is reprinted from its [::] marker (the window and the equipped lines only). Y on the row level leaves.
Exit: the B and Y latch bits are consumed (TRB $032B with $C0) and joy_pressed+1 is cleared; the scroll words, BG2SC, TM, CGADSUB and W12SEL are restored from the scene's shadows (tm_shadow, cgadsub_shadow, bg2sc_shadow, w12sel_shadow, stored by the scene loader), BG12NBA = 0; RestoreSceneBgGfxAndPalette, RestoreCgramBuffer and LoadEquippedMagicGfx put the field back in that order; when the equipped magic changed (menu_magic_on_open) all projectiles are killed and $0433 and $0434 cleared (OQ-I009-11); lib_player_helpers.ApplyPlayerWeaponPose restores the player's pose; BG3 is cleared, hud_dirty_flags = $1F, one sub-frame runs, the screen is switched on (INIDISP = $0F).

=== BG3 PAGE, ICONS ===
The BG3 text page is the 2 KB buffer at $7F7000 (bg3_tilemap_buffer), the BG2 icon page the buffer at $7F7800; vram_upload_flags bit 0 asks the NMI to send the BG3 page, bit 1 the icon page. DrawInventoryIcon writes four BG3 cells (selection frame tile $2A with its three flips, palette 3, when the slot has bit 7; else four zero cells) and the four words of the icon record IconTileRecords[id x 8] to the BG2 page (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right). ClearBg3Page and ClearBg3UpperHalf fill the page with $2000 (tile 0, priority) but set their upload bit with DBR = $7F, so the TSB reaches $7F:03B8 instead of vram_upload_flags (OQ-I027-1).

=== MENU TEXT, GEAR AND DESCRIPTIONS ===
StatusScreenText, SoulsScreenTitleText, the five soul lines, EquipMenuFrameText, ItemMenuFrameText and the description headers (the HUD strings HudFrameText .. EnemyGaugeText with the repeat counts in HudRepeatCounts are in lib_hud) are ASCIIString parts with text control codes (the renderer is lib_text_render, batch A6: [CUR:o] cursor to BG3 byte offset o, [07:w,h] window, [03:v] attribute, [06:n,addr] n packed BCD digits, [0B:t,&c] repeat tile t by the count byte at c, [TBL:list,addr] string number (word at addr) of a pointer list, [02:n] entry n of TextListPointers (0 and 1 are fixed six-tile labels, 2 = the player name at $1B92), [04:a,b] gauge from two words, [N] newline, [::] marks the re-entry point '+M', [JMP:&s] continue at s). The extractor prints the period glyph as '-' and an apostrophe as a space ('Goat s Food').
DescriptionTextList holds 65 string pointers, index = item id (0 = empty window). Every record starts [CUR:48A][TBL:&ItemNameList,&NameIndexCells + 2 x (id - 1)] (the item name on the first line; NameIndexCells holds k + 1 for entry k because [TBL] reads its index from memory). Weapons then print the minimum swing level from WeaponMinLevelBcd (two BCD digits at $4B2) and a bar of GearStatTable strength tiles; armors only a defence bar; magic and items start the text at $50A. Stub records (ids $2B-$31, $33, $34, $3B-$3F) print their own name and [JMP] into the carrying record (DescMastersEmblemA, DescRedHotMirror, DescBrownStone) at its [::] marker. The Gem costs of magic are literal text digits (4, 8, 8, 1, 8, 20, 8, 2; OQ-I009-10).
GearStatTable has two rows of 17 bytes indexed by item id: row 0 the strength bonus of weapons ids 1-8 (1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12), row 1 (+$11) the defence bonus of armor ids 9-$10 (the same numbers). RecalcGearStats adds the weapon and armor entries into gear_power and gear_defense. The minimum levels (1, 5, 11, 15, 16, 19, 22, 24) are compared by the player code (player_core) with player_level_bcd; the walkthrough weapon table lists exactly these. The item names (ItemNameList and its 65 strings, file offsets 85876-86757) are noted in the ItemNameList part (batch A8).

=== NOTES ===
- StoreInventoryEntry (file offset 73977, lib_inventory_store, batch A4) lies between ChooseItemSlot's neighbour routines: the code of this file continues at 74040 in lib_choice_menus.
- ROM item names differ from the walkthrough in a few places (OQ-I027-3); labels use the walkthrough names, the strings keep the ROM text.
- Sound requests: BRK #$07 follows every cursor move and page change, BRK #$18 every confirm (OQ-I009-12).
lib_name_entry_and_staff_roll:
The two text screens that the story scripts call: the name entry screen (RunNameEntryScreen) and the staff roll scroller (ScrollStaffRollText) (name entry code at file offsets 74990-75353 and strings at 83037-83222, SNES $02:A4EE-$A658 and $02:C45D-$C515; staff roll code at 75471-75625, SNES $02:A6CF-$A768; bank 02).

One file because both are small interactive text screens with their own loop and one caller each: RunNameEntryScreen from cop_items_stats_text, ScrollStaffRollText from the credits actor of gv_front_end. The sections below keep the notes of the two former files in file order.

Name entry screen (file offsets 74990-75353 code, 83037-83222 strings; SNES $02:A4EE-$A658 and $02:C45D-$C515, bank 02).

=== MODEL ===
RunNameEntryScreen is one blocking routine: Cop3A_EnterPlayerName calls it once, at the start of the game after the Master's first speech (walkthrough 01-in-the-beginning.md: 'You will then get to pick a name for yourself. Choose what you will; there is no default name to be used'). The code agrees: the buffer is not pre-filled; it only continues a name that is already in it (the loop at loc_0124FF finds the first 0 byte).
The screen is plain BG3 text, drawn with PrintTextString from three strings: NameEntryFrameText (prompt, window, name line, placeholders), NameEntryGridText (the letter grid) and NameEntryCloseText (erases the window). Every change repaints both strings, which also erases the old cursor.

=== STATE ===
- X = BG3 byte offset of the cursor cell, from $03C6 (the blank cell left of 'A'); the letter is the tile at X + 2 (bg3_tilemap_buffer + 2 + X).
- name_cursor_col ($0441, 0-12) and name_cursor_row ($0443, 0-4); both are zeroed on entry.
- Y = write pointer into the name buffer $1B92-$1B99 (8 characters). A character is accepted while Y < $1B9A; the 0 terminator is stored at [Y] when the name is finished, so a full name has its terminator at $1B9A (OQ-I010-13).

=== GRID ===
13 columns, two tiles (4 bytes) per column, five rows: A-M, N-Z, a-m, n-z, then 0-9, '-', the tile $24 (printed by the extractor as an arrow: backspace) and the tile $23 (printed as AE: accept). Rows are $80 apart (one text row is two tile rows); an extra $40 follows rows 1 and 3, so Up and Down add or subtract $C0 there and Down from row 4 / Up from row 0 wrap by $280. Right from column 12 wraps by -$30, Left from column 0 by +$30.

=== BUTTONS (joy_pressed+1 bits) ===
Right (0) MoveNameCursorRight, Left (1) MoveNameCursorLeft, Down (2) MoveNameCursorDown, Up (3) MoveNameCursorUp, Start (4) FinishNameEntry (an empty name is ignored), Select (5) ignored, Y (6) DeleteNameChar (ignored when empty), B (7) PickNameChar (the tile under the letter decides: $23 finish, $24 backspace, else append with sound $18). Every cursor move jumps to BlipAndRedrawNameEntry (sound $07, then redraw). After each redraw the screen waits for all buttons to be released, so one press is one step.

=== NOTES ===
- Sound ids $07 and $18 are BRK requests (OQ-I010-16).
- The save-slot name copy at $0447-$044E (list entry 3 of TextListPointers) is filled by DrawSaveSlotMenu from the save block, not by this screen.
- FM-A6 correction: in NameEntryFrameText the [09] (one-row font) comes after the name [02:2], so only the placeholders are one-row; the name line is two-row.

Staff roll (credits) scroller (file offsets 75471-75625, SNES $02:A6CF-$A768, bank 02).

=== MODEL ===
ScrollStaffRollText prints a long string line by line on BG3 while scrolling the layer. The only caller is the credits actor of gv_front_end (gv_obj_staff_roll_007638, Y = gv_epilogue_texts.StaffRollText, 'The staff of Soul Blazer ...'); afterwards the actor waits two COP 1B delays of $F0 frames and changes scene with COP 10. The walkthrough (08-world-of-evil.md) says only 'Enjoy the credits'; the credits text is not quoted there.
Each glyph is two tiles: tile c with attribute $21 (tile bit 8 set) at the write cell and tile c with attribute $20 one row below ((X + $40) & $7FF, wrapping inside the 2 KB page). [N] ($0D) scrolls scroll_bg3_y by 32 pixels, one pixel per RunSubFrame, moves the line start four tile rows down ((old + $100) & $7FF) and clears 128 words (four rows of tile 0, attribute $20) there. [14:n] moves the write cell right by n tiles. 0 ends.
The line start lives on the stack (one word, replaced on every [N]); the routine pops it at the end, so X is not preserved.

=== NOTES ===
- Whether the clear of the new line can overwrite a line still on screen, how long the roll runs and what the 8-bit scroll does when it wraps are open (OQ-I010-17, OQ-I010-12). Spelling oddities in the credits text are OQ-I010-11.
lib_scene_asset_loader:
Scene asset loader, Quintet LZ expander and boot hardware reset (file offsets 78281-78288 and 78450-80601, SNES $02:B1C9 and $02:B272-$BAD9, bank 02).

=== MODEL ===
Every scene change calls LoadSceneAssets once (lib_boot_and_scene_init InitSceneState), after the scene-change code has put the PPU in forced blank with NMI off. So every VRAM, CGRAM-buffer and WRAM write below happens without a vblank check. dp$2F-$31 is the long pointer to the asset list (SceneAssetLists, $05:8000), set once at boot by InitHardwareAndClearWram.
The asset list has one record per scene: area, scene, commands, then a 00 byte. FindSceneRecord walks the records from the top and stops at the first whose scene equals scene_current ($0316) and whose area equals area_current ($0314). The first record is a dummy (area $53, scene $59) with no commands and the list has no end sentinel (OQ-I011-3). The other 97 records are exactly the 97 scenes that have a scene profile.
A command byte has exactly one bit set. LoadSceneAssets reads one command at a time and tries the bits from $80 down to $01 (a BIT ladder), calls the handler, which reads its own operands with ReadAssetByte, and stops on a 00 byte:
  $80 graphics   6 operand bytes  b0 start, b1 end (512-byte units, b0 bit 7 = raw), b2 VRAM page (word address b2 << 8), 3-byte pointer. LoadSceneGraphics. Skipped when asset_skip_mask bit 3 is set
  $40 palette    6 operand bytes  b0 first source colour, b1 end colour, b2 destination colour, pointer. LoadScenePalette. Skip bit 2
  $20 tileset    7 operand bytes  b0 start, b1 end (64-byte units, b0 bit 7 = raw), b2 destination offset, b3 layer mask (1 BG1, 2 BG2), pointer. LoadMetatileDefs. Skip bit 1
  $10 tilemap    4 operand bytes  type (1 BG1, 2 BG2, 0 Mode 7), pointer. LoadSceneTilemap. Skip bit 0
  $08 asset8     1 operand byte   id below $80 = scene profile, $80-$BF = jump to the label id or $40, $C0-$FF = a label. ApplySceneProfile. Never skipped
  $04 meta4      3 operand bytes  ignored. SkipMeta4Command (no record uses it)
  $02 music      5 operand bytes  b0 start command, b1 variant, pointer. LoadSceneMusic. Skip bit 5
  $01 spritemap  6 operand bytes  b0 (0 = $7E:3800, else $7E:F000), b1 and b2 ignored, pointer. LoadSceneSpritemap. Skip bit 4
Shared segments are how scenes of one world share graphics: an asset8 jump (id $80-$BF) makes FindAssetLabel scan the whole list for the matching label ($C0-$FF) and the walk continues after that label in the OTHER record, up to that record's 00. The 65 jumps in the list go to 37 labels.

=== STREAM POINTERS AND CACHE ===
Every asset pointer in a record is a 3-byte linear FILE OFFSET (lo, mid, hi). ReadAssetPointer converts it to a LoROM address in dp$29-$2B: bank = offset >> 15, address = $8000 + (offset and $7FFF). Ten 3-byte cache cells at $0407-$0424 remember the pointer of the last asset loaded into a slot: graphics by VRAM page (asset_cache_gfx0-3 for b2 $00, $10, $20, $30), tileset per layer (asset_cache_tileset1/2), tilemap per layer (asset_cache_tilemap1/2), spritemap and music. CheckAssetCache compares the new pointer with the cell, stores it and says 'load' (carry set) only when different, so entering a scene that uses the same assets in the same slots costs nothing. Palettes have no cache. A graphics b2 other than $00/$10/$20/$30 ($40 and $FF), and a tileset or tilemap type other than 1 or 2, zero the cells of that kind and always load. A zeroed cell forces a reload: other code zeroes cells to invalidate them. The cache keys on the pointer only, not on the range (b0, b1); no two commands of the shipped list share a pointer with different ranges, so that hazard does not occur.
asset_skip_mask ($03B4) is a one-shot request: a cutscene script (or ReleaseLairAtSwitch for the return trip) writes $0020 just before its scene change so that the music is not reloaded, even when the warp goes to another world (15 writer sites in 10 files; the Phoenix scene of the Soul of Mountain House goes to the World of Evil this way), and InitSceneState clears it after the load. Skipped commands still advance Y past their operands. The record walkers (FindSceneRecord, FindAssetLabel) ignore the mask.

=== QUINTET LZ ===
DecompressQuintetLz is the Quintet LZ expander of corpus/gaia-core/quintet-lz.md: a 256-byte ring pre-filled with $20, first write position $EF, a flag bit per token (1 = literal byte, 0 = back reference of an 8-bit ring position and a 4-bit length, count = length + 2), bits read MSB first with the one-hot mask dp$1E. It does NOT read the 2-byte length word that precedes every compressed stream: each caller reads it into dp$23 first. The loader decompresses to $7E:6000 (graphics and tileset staging, 8 KB at most), $7E:C000 (Mode 7 map), $7E:3800 or $7E:F000 (spritemap) and the layer map pages.

=== SCENE PROFILE, MUSIC AND VARIANT ===
ApplySceneProfile writes the PPU layout of the scene from a 12-byte record of lib_scene_profile_data (see its block note for the layout) and sets location_id, world_index, the BG tile attributes, the view height, the parallax ratios, scene_variant and no_combat_scene. scene_variant ($031E) selects which music record of the scene plays: LoadSceneMusic plays a record only when its variant byte equals scene_variant. InitSceneState clears scene_variant after the load, so it is a one-shot request: an actor may set it before the scene change; otherwise LookupSceneVariant (lib_map_tile_patches) may set it from the switch rows of SceneVariantRules; otherwise bits 7 and 6 of profile byte 11 add 1 each. The profile command is always the first command of a record, so the variant is final before the music command runs.

=== NOTES ===
- The loader never sets dp$2E, the bank byte of the copy destination [dp$2C]. Its only writer is the SPC upload (engine_spc_ipl_upload: $07 at the start, incremented per bank, $7E at the end), so the tileset and raw map copies write to the bank left by the last music upload. Whether the very first scene after boot sees $7E is open (OQ-I011-1).
- LoadMapLayer stores the height byte of a raw map with its flag bit into map_height_px (OQ-I011-2). The raw tilemap and tileset flags look unused in the shipped data.
- The LZ ring is the page $7E:0100-$01FF, which every decompression overwrites (OQ-I011-8).
- Two BRA instructions never run (after eight ASL of a non-zero byte): FindSceneRecord ends its ladder with BRA GraphicsCacheHit and FindAssetLabel with BRA loc_0139E6, a STZ BG2HOFS inside InitHardwareAndClearWram (OQ-I011-10). They pin the layout: a rebuild that keeps the bytes needs those labels at the same relative distance, so InitHardwareAndClearWram cannot move away from FindAssetLabel on its own.
- Walkthrough check: the places and bosses the walkthrough names (Grass Valley, GreenWood, St. Elles, Mountain of Souls, Leo's Laboratory, Magridd's Castle, World of Evil, Deathtoll) agree with the location names that profile ids select (LocationNameList); the story text is not in the walkthrough.
lib_scene_profile_data:
Scene profile list and the 97 scene profile records (file offsets 92321-93740, SNES $02:E8A1-$EE2C, bank 02).

=== MODEL ===
A scene profile is a 12-byte record of video and game settings that a scene's asset record selects with an asset8 command whose id is below $80 (ApplySceneProfile in lib_scene_asset_loader). The id is also the location id (location_id, $1C6A): the pause banner uses it as the string number in LocationNameList. SceneProfileList holds 128 words, one per id: the bank-$02 address of the record, 0000 for the 31 ids that have none (25-27, 35-3B, 48-4F, 5D-63, 74-77, 7E-7F). The loader subtracts the list's own address from the word and indexes from the list label with long addressing. The records are not in id order (23 and 24 come before 19, 34 before 2E).

=== RECORD LAYOUT (12 bytes) ===
  +0   TM, also TMW and tm_shadow (main screen layers)
  +1   TS, also TSW (sub screen layers)
  +2   CGWSEL
  +3   CGADSUB, also cgadsub_shadow
  +4   flags: bit 0 sets tile_attr_bg1 = $2000, bit 1 sets tile_attr_bg2 = $2000, bits 4-5 go to scene_sprite_attr+1, bit 6 view height (set 256, clear 224), bit 7 clear adds bit 8 to the BG2 tile attribute word; bits 2-3 are never read (OQ-I011-7)
  +5   BG layout: bits 0-1 screen size of the first layer, bits 2-3 of the second, bit 7 swaps the layers (bg_scroll_swap = 1): BG1SC = ($70 if swapped else $60) + size, BG2SC = ($60 if swapped else $70) + size, so the map bases are VRAM words $6000 and $7000
  +6   BGMODE ($09 = Mode 1 with BG3 priority, $0F = Mode 7 for location $10)
  +7..+10  four parallax ratios for BG1 x, BG1 y, BG2 x, BG2 y: high nibble = numerator, low nibble = divisor ($11 = same speed, $12 = half speed, $00 = fixed)
  +11  bits 0-3 world_index, bit 5 no_combat_scene, bits 6 and 7 each add 1 to scene_variant

=== WORLDS ===
world_index 0 Grass Valley (ids 00-13: the village, the Underground Castle, Leo's Paintings, the dream rooms and the intro scenes), 1 GreenWood (14-24), 2 St. Elles (28-34), 3 Mountain of Souls (3C-47), 4 Leo's Laboratory (50-5C), 5 Magridd's Castle (64-73), 6 World of Evil (78-7D). The first id of each world (00, 14, 28, 3C, 50, 64, 78: the Master's shrine rooms) has byte 4 = $E4 and byte 5 = $0F; id 11 has the same two bytes.

=== NOTES ===
- Byte 11 = $A0 or $A1-$A5 (variant + 1, no combat) occurs exactly in the 12 dream rooms (A dream: Tulip, Lisa, Bird, Stump, a dolphin, Servas, an old man, a mushroom, a cat, a soldier and the two rooms the ROM names 'A dream 1'). Byte 11 = $C0-$C5 (variant + 2) occurs exactly in six rooms: Monster in the paintings (0C), Tomb of a stone statue (22), A ghost ship (32), Poseidon (44), Tin Doll (59) and The deck of an airship (72). SceneVariantRules has a variant-0 row for the same six locations. The likely meaning is boss music until the boss switch is set, then the normal tune (OQ-I011-5, OQ-I011-6).
- Locations 0F-13 have a profile but an empty name: they are the intro and transition scenes (00/09-00/0D, and 00/0A is the Mode 7 scene), which show no banner.
- The records are read once per scene load; no code reads them again, so the list and the records can move together.
lib_system_helpers:
System helpers of bank 02: the HDMA channel queue, the NMI and vblank switches with the screen-on step, and the boot PPU layout (file offsets 71774-71931, 78198-78280 and 80602-80678, SNES $02:985E-$98FB, $02:B176-$B1C8 and $02:BADA-$BB26).

The parts are ResetHdmaQueue, QueueHdmaIndirect, QueueHdmaDirect, EnableDisplayAndNmi, ForceBlankNmiOff, EnableNmi, DisableNmi, WaitVBlank and ApplyBootPpuLayout. EnableDisplayAndNmi (called by lib_menus) joined the NMI and vblank switches it belongs with; ApplyBootPpuLayout (called by engine_boot_main_loop at boot, after InitHardwareAndClearWram) joined as the other PPU-setup routine (it was the one-routine file lib_013ADA; it could not stay in the loader file and InitHardwareAndClearWram could not leave it, OQ-I042-7). The sections below keep the notes of the parts: the queue and the switches, then the boot layout.

HDMA channel queue and the NMI and vblank switches (file offsets 71774-71931 and 78220-78280, SNES $02:985E-$98FB and $02:B18C-$B1C8, bank 02).

=== HDMA CHANNEL QUEUE ===
HDMA channels 4-7 are handed out one per call within a frame; channels 0-2 are used by the NMI for OAM, CGRAM and VRAM transfers (HandleVBlank, engine_vblank_nmi). State lives in the direct page: dp$42 is the pending channel mask (the NMI copies it to HDMAEN), dp$44 the bit of the next free channel ($10 first), dp$46 the offset of that channel's register block from $4300 ($40 first, so channel 4 = $4340) and dp$48 is set to $6000 and never read. ResetHdmaQueue empties the queue at the start of every work phase. QueueHdmaDirect and QueueHdmaIndirect program the next channel; both are entered by long call with M = 8 and X = 16, take A.low = bank, B = PPU register index ($00-$3F, the low byte of the $21xx register) and Y = table address (load them with LDA #reg, XBA, LDA #bank, LDY #addr) and finish in the shared tail WriteHdmaChannelRegisters. HdmaDmapByRegister, indexed by the register number, supplies the DMA mode byte (one register, a register pair or the same register twice).
Indirect mode (DMAP or $40) sets both the table bank A1Bn and the indirect data bank DASBn to the bank given, so the table and the data it points to share one bank; every caller passes $7E and a WRAM table at $7800 or $7000. Direct mode reads the table as is (ROM tables gv_hdma_title_bgmode_006A86 and gv_hdma_gradient_table_01B284 or WRAM).
There is no overflow guard: the fourth call shifts $80 out of dp$44 and the carry that ADC #$10 then adds (there is no CLC) makes dp$46 = $81; a fifth call per frame would write $4381-$4387, which is not a DMA channel (OQ-I009-9).

=== NMI AND VBLANK ===
nmi_enabled ($03D2) is non-zero while the frame code runs with NMI on: EnableNmi increments it, EnableDisplayAndNmi increments it, DisableNmi and ForceBlankNmiOff zero it. The text renderer's input wait (lib_text_render.WaitFrameReadButtons) tests it: with NMI on it waits for the vblank, with NMI off it runs a whole sub-frame instead (RunSubFrame). WaitVBlank is the only wait for a vblank; when NMI is on, HandleVBlank runs inside it.

=== NOTES ===
- The extractor decoded ResetHdmaQueue with M = 16 (LDA #$8510 and MVP) until the M override at 71774; the real code is the 16 bytes shown now (OQ-I005-7).
- ForceBlankNmiOff, EnableNmi and DisableNmi are the NMI switches of the main loop and the scene change; their call sites are in engine_boot_main_loop, lib_menus, lib_boot_and_scene_init and engine_spawn_lairs_death_drops.
